On Sat, Mar 18, 2017 at 4:15 AM, Veranso Marie Claire <mario_...@yahoo.ca> wrote:
Dear Nicholas,
I am a PhD student and trying to get my way round R and BiogeoBears, which I think is quite interesting. I have been able to use my own data and run it to the end successfully but for the plot area probability.
I have also tried  this immediately after running the DEC and DEC+J models using the example file data (Psychotria) but I get an error message every time after the command

add_per_area_probs_to_corners(tr, probs_each_area, left_or_right="left", cols_each_area=TRUE, barwidth_proportion=split_reduce_x*barwidth_proportion, barheight_proportion=split_reduce_y*barheight_proportion, offset_nodenums=offset_nodenums, offset_xvals=offset_xvals, offset_yvals=offset_yvals, root.edge=root.edge)

Here is the error message 
Error in file(filename, "r", encoding = encoding) : 
  cannot open the connection
 
In addition: Warning message:
In file(filename, "r", encoding = encoding) :
  cannot open file 'C:\Dropbox\_njm\__packages\BioGeoBEARS_setup\inst\extdata\a_scripts\plot_phylo3_nodecoords.R': No such file or directory


Hi Marie,

I'm not sure what script you are using?  That command is not in the default example script, the most up-to-date version of which is here:
http://phylo.wikidot.com/biogeobears#script

Anyway, the explanation is that, due to some obscure fight between APE and CRAN, I couldn't use an internal APE C function in BioGeoBEARS to get the corner coordinates to plot on.  

To get around that, I included a little extra script in BioGeoBEARS to find node corner coordinates.  The script is found with:

scriptdir = np(system.file("extdata/a_scripts", package="BioGeoBEARS"))

This should find your "extdata/a_scripts" directory inside of your BioGeoBEARS installation.  The example data files are also in "extdata".  If "scriptdir" produces something with "C:\Dropbox\_njm\__packages\BioGeoBEARS_setup\inst\extdata\", then it is referring to a directory on my old development computer from years ago, which doesn't help you!

Basically, make sure "scriptdir" refers to an actual directory on your own machine, and make sure the file "plot_phylo3_nodecoords.R" is in there.

Cheers,
Nick

P.S.: More background, from example script:

==============
#######################################################
# SETUP: Extension data directory
#######################################################
# When R packages contain extra files, they are stored in the "extdata" directory 
# inside the installed package.
#
# BioGeoBEARS contains various example files and scripts in its extdata directory.
# 
# Each computer operating system might install BioGeoBEARS in a different place, 
# depending on your OS and settings. 
# 
# However, you can find the extdata directory like this:
extdata_dir = np(system.file("extdata", package="BioGeoBEARS"))
extdata_dir
list.files(extdata_dir)

# "system.file" looks in the directory of a specified package (in this case BioGeoBEARS)
# The function "np" is just a shortcut for normalizePath(), which converts the 
# path to the format appropriate for your system (e.g., Mac/Linux use "/", but 
# Windows uses "\\", if memory serves).

# Even when using your own data files, you should KEEP these commands in your 
# script, since the plot_BioGeoBEARS_results function needs a script from the 
# extdata directory to calculate the positions of "corners" on the plot. This cannot
# be made into a straight up BioGeoBEARS function because it uses C routines 
# from the package APE which do not pass R CMD check for some reason.

==============

 

 Please can you help me. I have tried to read through the Biogeoears google group but I did not get any possible solutions.

Many Thanks
Marie Claire

parts:
It sounds like you are trying to use stuff inside of plot_BioGeoBEARS_results().  To do this, you may have to manually specify the value of "scriptdir", which is supposed to be the directory where plot_phylo3_nodecoords.R is on YOUR system.

These commands will help you figure out where plot_phylo3_nodecoords.R is:

# Find out where the extdata directory is in your BioGeoBEARS install:
system.file("extdata", package="BioGeoBEARS")

# Open that directory in your system's file explorer:
directory_to_open = system.file("extdata", package="BioGeoBEARS")

# Write a command for your system's operating system
command_text = paste0("open ", directory_to_open)

# Send the command to the operating system
system(commend_text)

# Now, a file-exploration window should open, and you can SEE the actual extdata directory, and the location of the a_scripts subdirectory.


In the main example script, this is supposed to fill in scriptdir, but either you've missed it somehow, or it's not working on your machine:

# See the example script, search for:
# http://phylo.wikidot.com/biogeobears#script
scriptdir = np(system.file("extdata/a_scripts", package="BioGeoBEARS"))

Cheers,
Nick

Hi Vhon,

I'm glad you worked it out.  Another option would be to just hit "3: None", so that it doesn't try to re-install other packages. It would still update BioGeoBEARS.

BioGeoBEARS depends on packages "rexpokit" and "cladoRcpp" which contains FORTRAN code from the FORTRAN library EXPOKIT, and C++ code.  To install these from GitHub you would need to have the gcc and gfortran compilers installed on your system.  This is quite a project to do.  

It is much easier to install rexpokit and cladoRcpp from CRAN, which has precompiled binaries available, so no compilers are needed on your end.

Cheers,
Nick

Hi Marie,

 

I'm not sure what script you are using?  That command is not in the default example script, the most up-to-date version of which is here:

http://phylo.wikidot.com/biogeobears#script

 

Anyway, the explanation is that, due to some obscure fight between APE and CRAN, I couldn't use an internal APE C function in BioGeoBEARS to get the corner coordinates to plot on.  

 

To get around that, I included a little extra script in BioGeoBEARS to find node corner coordinates.  The script is found with:

 

scriptdir = np(system.file("extdata/a_scripts", package="BioGeoBEARS"))

 

This should find your "extdata/a_scripts" directory inside of your BioGeoBEARS installation.  The example data files are also in "extdata".  If "scriptdir" produces something with "C:\Dropbox\_njm\__packages\BioGeoBEARS_setup\inst\extdata\", then it is referring to a directory on my old development computer from years ago, which doesn't help you!

 

Basically, make sure "scriptdir" refers to an actual directory on your own machine, and make sure the file "plot_phylo3_nodecoords.R" is in there.

 

Cheers,

Nick

 

P.S.: More background, from example script:
